name: Agent
effect: You work for an intelligence agency or a secret organization of your choice as a field agent or as an informant. You can access restricted information, request backup or borrow faction tech once per session. All contact with your organization is via secret dead drops, shady cantinas or anonymous kawah stands. Getting a reply might therefore take up to 24 hours. The GM decides if your request for help will be granted or not.

name: Agitator
effect:
You are very skilled in riling up or engaging with the masses. Regardless of your Reputation, they look up to you and whenever you speak before a crowd, you get the following bonuses to COMMAND or PERSUASION:
5-25 people = +1, 25–50 people = +2, 50+ people = +3.

name: Atmospheric Pilot
effect: Gives a +1 modifier to PILOT rolls when flying a vehicle in atmosphere (including a starship).

name: Authority
effect: By invoking your authority you can use your COMMAND skill instead of PERSUASION to get someone to bend to your will. This is situational and is up to the GM.

name: Banter
effect: Between fights, you release the tension in your team with some friendly banter. You and everyone in SHORT range of you, recover a Stress Point after a stretch if you are in a safe location. This can only occur after a conflict and only once per conflict. Multiple people with the talent does not stack.

name: Biochemist
effect: You can concentrate natural toxins, manufacture synthetic opioids or weaponize infections and viruses. Test science for each dose created. Lab access grants a +1 and increases the strength cap by 1. Each extra success rolled either increases the strength of the toxin by 1 (unless already at max strength cap) or gives you D6 extra doses. Common opioids like kambra, opor and arrash immediately give D6 doses at a successful roll. The resources needed will usually cost about 10% of the finished product’s market price and requires a suitable lab with the time to make them.

name: Blessing
effect: Once per session, you can bless another person by testing EMPATHY (may be pushed). Each six on the roll gives the target of the blessing a +1 to a roll at a later time. Unspent blessed sixes disappear after 24 hours. The receiver of the blessing must be within Close range of you. In combat, imparting the blessing is a slow action. Instead, you can also create and bless a talisman for that day. The process takes D6 hours and requires a chapel or an altar. A talisman provides a +1 to a skill test, then the blessing wears off. Only one talisman is allowed per character to be active at one time.

name: Bodyguard
effect: If someone within CLOSE range of you is hit by an attack, you can dive in to take the hit. Roll for MOBILITY. It doesn’t count as an action in combat. If you roll one or more successes you take the hit instead. This roll can be pushed.

name: Born Leader
effect: You exude authority, from your personality, your position, your place on the command team or because the force of law is behind you. If you fail a COMMAND roll you can immediately, as a free action, attempt a PERSUASION roll to try and salvage the situation.

name: Brawler
effect: Gives you a +1 modifier to MELEE COMBAT rolls in unarmed melee combat. Your unarmed MELEE COMBAT attacks have a CRIT threshold of 3 instead of 4.

name: Bypass
effect: You have experience jury-rigging tool- kits and using diagnostic devices to hack doors. You gain a +1 modification to the TECHNOLOGY skill when attempting to unlock a locked entryway or gain access to a location you cannot enter.

name: Calming Presence
effect: People find themselves relaxing whenever you are around. Once per day if someone spends a shift taking a Rest in your presence, they recover 1 additional Stress Point.

name: Close Combat Specialist
effect: Gives a +1 modifier to RANGED COMBAT rolls for firing pistols, submachine guns and shotguns. Also gives a +1 modifier to RANGED COMBAT rolls made to reload these firearms (page 65).

name: Combat Medic
effect: Gives a +1 modifier to MEDICAL AID rolls for helping a character incapacitated by physical damage get back up (page 73) or for treating infection and disease in the field.

name: Combat Veteran
effect: You draw two cards for initiative, and choose the best one. If you also have Accelerated Reflexes, you get to an additional card and choose the best one.

name: Compassion
effect: This isn’t just a job for you. You truly care about the people under your care. When you push any skill roll based on EMPATHY, you can roll with a +1 modifier.

name: Cunning
effect: If your training has taught you anything, it’s to always be on the lookout for anything that can give you an edge. When you push any skill roll based on WITS, you can roll with a +1 modifier.

name: Dodge
effect: When attacked in melee combat, you can dodge as a free action once per turn. This works like Defending in Melee combat but you roll using MOBILITY instead of MELEE COMBAT and you can only use it to reduce damage (not counterattack or disarm).

name: Exo Specialist
effect: You get a +1 to MOBILITY and FORCE when using an exo of any kind – from loaders to battle exos.

name: Faction Honors (GM awarded)
effect: You have strong connections with a faction and are either considered to be an honorary member or as very trustworthy by both the rank-and-file and the leadership. You get a +1 to any rolls when dealing with people who are either allies of, or fear, the faction because of your reputation among them. This can be taken or earned from multiple factions but must be purchased as a separate talent for each.

name: Faction Standing (GM Awarded)
effect: You belong to a faction or a gang and can use its reputation to get a +1 to PERSUASION when trying to scare or threaten someone – given that the person you are threatening knows of the faction, and that the faction has some influence in the location where you are.

name: Field Commander
effect: You can use COMMAND to give orders in combat as a fast action instead of a slow action. You can choose to save additional fast actions to issue a new command as a reaction at a later point in the round or issue two or more commands in a single turn. Each COMMAND requires a separate roll and has a separate modifier.

name: Flyweight
effect: When you attack or defend in melee combat, you can use AGILITY instead of STRENGTH.

name: Frontline Leader
effect: Roll COMMAND when you spot enemy troops, vehicles, and weapons. If you succeed, the Referee should tell you their general stats.

name: Full Throttle
effect: You like to go fast. Really fast. When piloting a spacecraft, atmospheric flyer or ground vehicle capable of high speeds you get a +1 modification to PILOT rolls for any Accelerate or Decelerate actions and when driving at or close to maximum speed.

name: Gearhead
effect: With a successful TECHNOLOGY test, you can repair an item or jury-rig a one-use contraption for a specific task. The number of successes on your roll determines the Reliability of the item (max 3) but is dependent on available materials, time, etc. If doing a repair, the recovered Reliability will only last for a shift and then reverts back to it’s original rating (if not reduced by then).

name: Ground Vehicle Specialist
effect: Gives a +1 modifier to PILOT all ground vehicles.

name: Group Psychology
effect: You understand what drives pack behavior and how people tend to function as a group. With a successful OBSERVATION roll you can predict the short-term attitude or behavior of a group of people. You get to ask the GM a question about the group, and they must offer you some insight (more detail with extra successes) into what they are going to do as a group.

name: Gunsmith
effect: You gain a +1 to TECHNOLOGY when it comes to making, modifying or repairing guns and ammunition.

name: Hardened
effect: Long years of danger and conflict have hardened you, giving you 1 additional Stress Point. This can be taken twice.

name: Hard Hitter
effect: You get a +2 modification to MELEE COMBAT if you spend a fast action to line up the attack. If the defender attempts to block, they receive a -1 to the roll.

name: Heavy Weapons Expert
effect: The military uses a variety of heavy weapons, from plasma guns to tactical missiles and tank guns. You get a +1 modification to RANGED COMBAT when firing such weapons, and +1 when attempting to unjam or fix a heavy weapon. This affects man-portable heavy weapons up to vehicle mounted and artillery.

name: Historian
effect: Roll OBSERVATION when you arrive at a new location. If you succeed, the Referee can tell you something significant that has happened here in the past (if anything ever did).

name: Hold Your Nerve
effect: Your resilience allows you to block out the bad things going on around you. Once per day you can use a specific item of sentimental value to make an EMPATHY roll. Any successes immediately reduce your stress by the number of successes rolled.

name: Hug the Dirt
effect: With this talent you’re able to maximize cover from incoming ranged attacks and return effective fire when you’re down on the ground. Attacks against you while prone are at -2 (instead of -1) and you get a +2 fire support bonus (instead of +1). All other rules for being prone apply as normal.

name: Influence
effect: With rank, experience or talent comes certain privileges—being obeyed is one of them. You can push any skill roll based on EMPATHY twice, not just once. All other rules for rolling 1’s and stress apply, with this adding an automatic 1 point of stress.

name: Inquisitive
effect: You are always seeking to expand the boundaries of your knowledge. When you push any skill roll based on WITS, you can choose to add +1 to the re-roll.

name: Intelligence Training
effect: Roll OBSERVATION when you spot an enemy force. If you succeed, the Referee must tell you something useful about their current organization and objectives.

name: Intense Focus
effect: Your discipline and attention to detail gives you the ability to block out the outside world and focus on the task at hand. You gain a +1 modification to any task that takes at least a stretch (10 minutes) or longer complete, but if you are interrupted you automatically fail the task and must start again.

name: Investigator
effect: You see what others miss, and are skilled at noticing small details and making sense of them. When you spend a Turn in a room or similar location, you can roll for OBSERVATION. Only one attempt is allowed (cannot push). For each success you roll, you may ask the GM one of the following questions. The GM must answer truthfully, but is allowed to give vague or incomplete information. What happened here? Is there anything hidden here, and if so, where? Are there any details here that are out of place, something that’s out of the ordinary?

name: Judge of Character
effect: You can tell if someone is lying or telling the truth without testing PERSUASION if your EMPATHY and MANIPIULATION are higher than the person you’re judging. It takes about a minute and you can’t tell any details, only whether the person is lying or not.

name: Killer
effect: You can kill an incapacitated person outright without suffering any negative effect (Pg 73)

name: Licensed
effect: You have the proper licenses to buy restricted gear and weapons). You can purchase the items if you can afford them, and if they are available at your location. Being licensed is not the same as being permitted to carry all kinds of weaponry in public, however. Local regulations can still stop you from carrying weapons you are allowed to own.

name: Like the Back of Your Hand
effect: This vehicle is yours, and you know every bolt and cable, nook and cranny. Choose one vehicle or spacecraft (not one type, but a single, specific craft). You get a +1 modification to PILOT with the chosen vehicle. You can choose this talent several times, once for each vehicle (such as a spacecraft and a shuttle). If you happen to lose your specific vehicle, you can spend a week getting to know a new vehicle with this talent.

name: Linguist
effect: You know another language of your choice, well enough to be taken as native on a successful PERSUASION roll.

name: Load Carrier
effect: You can carry two additional encumbrance units in your combat gear and two more in your backpack.

name: Martial Artist
effect: Your Melee combat unarmed attacks have their CRIT rating reduced by 1. You can also make an unarmed attack as a FAST action but at a -2.

name: Melee Specialist
effect: Gives you a +1 modifier to MELEE COMBAT rolls for all hand-to-hand combat weapons, such as knives, bayonets, and clubs.

name: Menacing
effect: You have a scary physical presence that makes it easy to intimidate people. You can roll for PERSUASION using STRENGTH instead of EMPATHY when you threaten someone to make them do what you want. If you succeed, your opponent cannot demand anything in return from you. They can still choose to attack you instead of giving in.

name: Merciless
effect: You can perform a coup de grace without rolling for EMPATHY. Also, you recover 1 stress from killing an enemy but cannot happen more than once per day.

name: Navigator
effect: When setting course of travel in a spaceship, roll DATA DJINN. For each success rolled, the duration of the trip is reduced by 10% (round off to the nearest whole number of days up or down).

name: Nerves of Steel
effect: You keep a cool head in all situations. When you drop to zero Stress Points, you recover 1 Stress Point. This cannot occur more than once per session.

name: Nine Lives
effect: No matter how bad it looks, you always seem to come out of situations alive. When you suffer a critical injury, you may roll two dice and choose the lower result.

name: Nurse
effect: When you tend to a character recovering from a critical injury, each day counts double for each shift spent per day. You can tend to a number of patients equal to your MEDICAL AID skill level (D-1, C-2, B-3, A-4)

name: Past the Limit
effect: When the going gets tough, the tough get going, and you’re the toughest badass around. You can re-roll a single 1 on any non-combat skill roll based on STRENGTH. This re-roll can be on the initial roll or the re-roll but must be declared you’re using this feat.

name: Pinpoint
effect: Gives a +1 modifier to MOBILITY rolls for thrown weapons, including knives and grenades. If you push the roll, you can ignore a single 1 that is rolled.

name: Point Blank
effect: The penalty for shooting in melee combat (page 63 in the Player’s Manual) is reduced one step, i.e. no penalty for pistols, carbines and SMGs, and -1 for other ranged weapons.

name: Precise Shooter
effect: When rolling ammo dice and counting up total bullets used, you can ignore one ammo die if rolling two or more ammo dice on the roll.

name: Quick Draw
effect: You can draw a weapon that is rifle sized or smaller so quickly it doesn’t cost you an action. If your weapon is already drawn when combat starts, you gain a +1 to your first shot(s) fired if you shoot in the first round.

name: Quick Healer
effect: You are very resilient and recover quickly from injuries. The healing time of critical injuries is halved for you.

name: Ranger
effect: Gives a +1 modifier when using SURVIVAL rolls for navigation, foraging and hunting in wild environments.

name: Rapid Reload
effect: You can reload a weapon as a fast action if your Ranged Combat roll fails. If you succeed, this counts as a free action.

name: Reaction Shot
effect: If an enemy makes a ranged attack against you, you are in close range, are aware of the enemy and have an action available you may as a quick action (reaction) try to shoot them first. Take +1 Stress, then roll for both attacks simultaneously. The shot with the most successes goes off first. If both shots hit, the second shot is aborted if the shooter is broken. If both shots roll the same amount of successes, both hit at the same time.

name: Reckless
effect: You live for the rush of adrenaline through your veins, pushing harder than others dare. When you push any skill roll based on AGILITY you can choose to add +1 to the re-roll.

name: Relentless
effect: At the cost of 1 Stress, you can gain one additional fast action. This can only be used once per combat.

name: Remote
effect: You are qualified to set up, control and repair remote sentry guns and other remotely- controlled battlefield devices, and to pilot remote vehicles. Receive +1 to rolls to carry out these tasks. The correct equipment is needed in all cases.

name: Resilient
effect: Roll for STRENGTH (attribute only) any time you suffer physical damage. You can’t push the roll, which does not count as an action. For every success you roll, one point of damage is eliminated at the cost of 1 Stress instead. If broken by Stress, additional damage is taken normally.

name: Rifle Specialist
effect: Gives a +1 modifier to RANGED COMBAT rolls for firing assault rifles and carbines. Also gives a +1 modifier to RANGED COMBAT rolls made to reload these firearms (page 65).

name: Robust
effect: You may ignore one critical injury effect at the cost of 1 HP (on top of any damage taken). You must activate this talent before the critical injury roll. Once used you must sleep at least one shift to be able to use the talent again.

name: Rugged
effect: You are used to extreme weather and other hardships (cold, storms, strong gravity, fire, etc). Gives you a +1 modifier to STAMINA rolls made for marching, resisting hypothermia, and other hardships.

name: Second Wind
effect: When you are reduced to zero HP, you can get back on your feet immediately, without anyone giving you first aid. Roll for STAMINA. For every success you roll, you recover 1 Hit Capacity and can keep fighting a little while longer. Once used, you must sleep at least one shift to be able to use the talent again. This talent has no effect if you suffered a critical injury as a part of being reduced to zero HP. This talent does not stack with the Adrenal Pump cyberware.

name: Seductive
effect: You have an eye for romance, and get a +1 to PERSUASION in situations when you try to achieve something through seduction, flirting or otherwise using your personal charisma to get someone to do what you want.

name: Soothing
effect: You read others as if they were open books, and possess a natural quality that makes people open up to you. You get a +1 to MEDICAL AID when treating someone who has been broken by stress. They also gain a +1 when using MEDICAL AID to counsel someone affected by a mental trauma.

name: Sniper
effect: Gives a +1 modifier to RANGED COMBAT rolls for firing marksman rifles. Also gives a +1 modifier to RANGED COMBAT rolls made to reload these firearms (page 65).

name: Spaceship Commander
effect: In the role as a captain of a spaceship during space combat, you can draw two initiative cards using the Initiative phase of space combat. Choose the one you want to use. You also gain a +1 to you COMMAND roll during the COMMAND phase.

name: Spaceship Gunner
effect: As a gunner on a spaceship during combat, you get a +1 modification to your HEAVY WEAPONS rolls for any ship-based weapon attacks.

name: Spaceship Mechanic
effect: You get a +1 modification when you use TECHNOLOGY or DATA DJINN to modify, upgrade or repair damage to a spacecraft.

name: Sprinter
effect: Gives a +1 bonus to MOBILITY rolls for running both in combat and out of combat.

name: Stealthy
effect: You get a +2 modification to INFILTRATION when using the skill to move undetected. This talent is only used if you are alone or everyone in the group has the talent.

name: Stoic
effect: You can roll for FORCE or STAMINA using WITS instead of STRENGTH.

name: Surgeon
effect: Gives a +2 modifier to MEDICAL AID rolls for treating critical injuries if the injured person is treated in a medical facility with the right tools.

name: Survivor
effect: You get +2 dice to all death rolls.

name: Take Control
effect: You know how to make people do what you want, and you don't feel bad about doing it. You can roll for PERSUASION using WITS instead of EMPATHY Gives a +1 bonus to COMMAND rolls for helping someone who is incapacitated by stress (page 77). Does not affect unit morale.

name: Talk Their Language
effect: A born orator and public speaker, you can talk to a crowd and make every person think you are talking just to them, and them alone. Rather than suffering a negative modifier to your COMMAND or PERSUASION rolls when out-numbered, you gain a +1 modification instead.

name: The Hassassin’s Thrust
effect: You are a highly trained assassin. When you make a sneak attack using a small weapon, you get +1 to MELEE COMBAT and reduce the CRIT threshold of the weapon by 1. Only affects weapons that weigh 1/2 or less (such as knives)

name: Third Eye
effect: You have the ability to sense an ambush, and once per session you can avoid the effects of being surprised. The talent also gives you a constant +1 to OBSERVATION when trying to detect a sneak attack or an ambush.

name: Tough
effect: You are used to taking a beating. You get 1 additional Hit Capacity. This can be taken twice

name: True Grit
effect: Life on the Frontier is a constant struggle. Luckily, you have what it takes to overcome anything that comes your way. When you re-roll any skill roll based on STRENGTH, you can add +1 to the re-roll.

name: Wealthy Family
effect: You can use the rumors of your family’s vast riches to give yourself a +1 to PERSUASION in any situation where the GM deems it relevant. Whether the rumors are true or not doesn’t matter. You can only choose this talent if you come from a Privileged background (page 21).

name: Weapon Specialist
effect: You’re an expert at using a specific weapon model – choose one from the weapon lists. When you use this weapon, you get +2 dice. You can choose this talent several times, once per weapon model (including unarmed). This talent stacks with other broad weapon talents like Close Combat Specialist, Rifle Specialist and Sniper.

name: Well Connected
effect: When visiting new locations, you always find lucrative contacts willing to help you out. The talent may be used once per visit to a station or a city. Your new contact can supply you with business opportunities or protection, or introduce you to local rulers — your choice

name: Zero-G Training
effect: Your sense of balance is well adapted to an environment without gravity or you have been specially trained to work in zero-g. You do not suffer the effects of Zero Gravity.

name: A Nose for Birr
effect: When trading, you get a +2 to PERSUASION. One use per session for the whole group (not once per PC).

name: Everything is for Sale
effect: You have a knack for finding the most corrupt public servants, toll officers or guards, and always get a +2 to PERSUASION when you are bribing someone.

name: Quickest Route
effect: You find the quickest route. Travel takes half the amount of time (page 138), or one encounter along the way may be ignored.

name: Assault
effect: You get a +1 to RANGED COMBAT, but only when everyone in the group attacks the same target in the same turn.

name: Charge
effect: You get a +2 to MOBILITY but only when everyone in the group, in the same turn, also spends at least one fast action on movement. The bonus lasts one turn only. Can be used once per session.

name: Situational Awareness
effect: You always know your surroundings, and get a +2 to OBSERVATION when testing it to discover an ambush.

name: Strategic Movement
effect: Your group is trained for anything. If one member of your team succeeds on a COMMAND roll (once per turn), they may allow a member of the squad to get 1 additional Fast Action to spend on finding cover or performing a movement action. The extra fast action can be used when the soldier is up to act in the turn order or as a reaction immediately after the COMMAND role succeeding.

name: A Friend in Every Port
effect: You can find a useful contact in a new place. The contact can protect you, lend you gear, or vouch for you with the local rulers. This can be used once per story arc.

name: Assassin’s Guild
effect: You can test INFILTRATION instead of MELEE COMBAT when you make a MELEE COMBAT attack against an enemy who isn’t aware of you.

name: Dancers of Ahlam
effect: You can test MOBILITY instead of PERSUASION when trying to make a good impression.

name: Seasoned Travelers
effect: You can test PERSUASION instead of CULTURE to understand a group’s customs.

name: Survivors
effect: You can get out of a dangerous situation somehow connected to nature, such as a brushfire or explosive decompression. The whole group escapes the danger. One use per session for the whole group (not once per PC).

name: Truth Seekers
effect: You can find important information or get a clue from the GM without rolling dice. The information must be important enough to enable you to overcome a minor obstacle or a challenge in the scenario. One use per session for the whole group (not once per PC).

name: Last Laugh
effect: You can get yourselves out of a pinch using your knack for entertainment. The GM gets 1 DP per use. One use per session for the whole group (not once per PC).

name: Mercy of the Icons
effect: When you are in a tight spot, the Icons will hear you. This means that you can cancel the effects of Darkness Points that have just been spent by the GM (Chapter 3). One use per session for the whole group (not once per PC).

name: One Last Birr
effect: You can make a living out of your craft or performances. Test MOBILITY instead of PERSUASION to find basic subsistence (food, drink, repairs – no new gear) when in a new place.

name: The Lady of Tears Talent
effect: You can get back up after having been broken by damage or stress, and are immediately restored to 1 HP remaining at the cost of 1 Stress. Alternatively, you can ignore the effects of a non-fatal Critical Injury for 1 stretch at the cost of 1 Stress.

name: The Dancer’s Talent
effect: You can evade an incoming attack, taking no damage. You can choose to activate the talent after a successful attack roll against you, but before the GM has revealed the effect. This causes 1 Stress per use.

name: The Gambler’s Talent
effect: You are incredibly lucky and can choose an automatic success on a non-combat skill test of your choice before rolling. It counts as if you had rolled a single success. If it is an advanced skill, you still need a level of at least 1 in that skill to activate the talent. This causes 1 Stress per use.

name: The Merchant’s Talent
effect: You can find a favorable loan enabling you to purchase an expensive object or a ship module. The loan must then be paid back within the agreed upon timeframe. This causes Stress equal to the amount of the loan, determined by the GM. Failure to pay back the loan causes a permanent point of stress until the loan is repaid.

name: The Deckhand’s Talent
effect: If your ship drops to zero Hull Points or Energy Points, you can restore D6 points of either kind instantly. This requires no action from you – it is the Icons intervening on your behalf. This causes 1 point of Stress.

name: The Traveler’s Talent
effect: You can ask the GM about a choice you have to make in the game. It has to be a choice with only two options. The GM must then answer truthfully which of the two is most beneficial to you, if that is at all possible to estimate. This causes 1 point of Stress.

name: The Messenger’s Talent
effect: You can make someone obey you, through careful words and actions, without having to test PERSUASION, but guarantees only a single success. Can be used on both NPCs and PCs. Your wish must be reasonable, you cannot, for example, force an NPC to act completely against their own interests. This causes 1 point of Stress.

name: The Judge’s Talent
effect: You deal an automatic critical injury when your attack hits, as long as the target suffered at least 1 point of damage after armor and cover. Any other effects from the attack are resolved as usual. This causes 1 point of Stress.

name: The Faceless One’s Talent
effect: Fate is on your side, giving you the benefit of getting to change a single, concrete detail in a scene more to your favor. It must be something that has a cosmetic or indirectly helpful effect – you cannot make an enemy disappear, but you can decide that there is a knife within reach, or that a window has been left open. The GM has final say on what is possible to accomplish with the talent. This causes 1 point of Stress.

name: Accelerated Reflexes
effect:
Your nerves are cybernetically modified with extra wiring and micro djinn, giving you superb body control. You get a +1 to MOBILITY for acrobatic maneuvers, and you get to roll your initiative with two cards and pick the best one to determine your initiative score. If you also have the Combat Veteran talent, you get three cards and choose the best one.
Cost: 7,000 birr.

name: Active Sensors
effect:
Active sensors are implanted in your body. You can use them like the active mode on a personal sensor whenever you wish. Details for sensors are found in Equipment
Cost: 3,000 birr.

name: Adaptive Cybernetic Eye
effect: You gain a +1 to TECHNOLOGY when making fine repairs, and a +1 to RANGED COMBAT and OBSERVATION (Fast action to activate) for the next turn. $10,000 birr.

name: Adrenal Pump
effect: A chemical injector pumps adrenaline and hormones into your bloodstream to regulate mood and reaction time. If Broken by either stress or damage, you may use one fast action in the following turn to roll STAMINA. Each success rolled restores 1 point of the Broken stat. Takes at least 24 hours to refresh once activated. You also gets a +1 to FORCE and MANIPULATE to resist torture or interrogation. 20,000 birr

name: Beautiful
effect:
Your beauty is breathtaking. Whether by classical standards or tasteful originality, you turn heads wherever you go. Your biosculpted looks give you a +1 to PERSUASION whenever they can affect the situation. People with the appropriate sexual orientation tend to fall in love with you. If you are in a place with different ideals of beauty, the GM may decide to ignore your modifier.
Cost: 25,000 birr.

name: Body Armor
effect:
You are cybernetically armored, giving you an extra Armor Rating of 1 to one hit location. The implant’s rating is added to any other armor you may wear as well. The implants give you a -1 penalty to MOBILITY for acrobatic maneuvers.
Cost: 6,000 birr.

name: Built-in Weapon (CYB)
effect:
You have a built-in weapon. The weapon is hard to detect and can only be discovered by someone actively searching for it. The weapon itself must be bought separately. To “draw” a built-in weapon is a fast action.
Cost: 3,000 birr.

name: Built-in Weapon (BIO)
effect:
You have a built-in weapon that counts as a primitive melee weapon (for example claws, a shorter blade or throwing knives). The weapon is very discreet and only a thorough medical check-up can discover it. “Drawing” this built-in weapon is a free action.
Cost: 40,000 birr.

name: Com Link
effect:
You have a built-in communications device, similar to a personal communicator. The benefit of the link is that it is very hard to detect – you can verbalize your message in your mind, and the receiver is jacked directly into your auditory system.
Cost: 1,500 birr.

name: Cybernetic Muscles
effect:
Muscles enhanced with ceramic fibers make you an extremely fast and strong runner. Your Movement Rate is increased by 1 hex to move in a round but only once per round (can be combined with Sprinter but not with Quick Reflexes). The critical rating of your unarmed attacks is decreased by 1.
Cost: 7,000 birr.

name: Endo Skeleton
effect:
An endo skeleton with powerful hydraulics and strong alloys supports your body, making you considerably stronger than others – you get a +1 to FORCE for heavy lifting. Your combat carrying capacity is increased by 2.
Cost: 7,000 birr.

name: Intelligent
effect:
Your brain’s bio code and cognitive pathways have been altered to make you cold and logical. You get a +1 to all SCIENCE and TECHNOLOGY tests, but a -1 to PERSUASION.
Cost: 25,000 birr.

name: Kinetic Absorption
effect:
The muscles or your skin have been enhanced with alloys or micro djinn that regenerate within seconds if damaged by trauma, explosions, fire or acid. This gives you an ablative armor that automatically reduces the first wound you receive each combat by 1. It takes about an hour for the process to cycle through and become active again. The cybernetics version of this talent requires extremely straining surgery, tripling the normal recovery time.
Cost: 30,000 birr (BIO),12,000 birr (CYB).

name: Language Modulator
effect:
Your larynx and vocal chords have been replaced with a sound modulator and an interpreter unit. You can automatically translate your speech to another language if you speak slowly. The modulator supports up to five different language packs. See Language Unit for more details.
Cost: 12,000 birr.

name: Lie Detector
effect:
You have a built-in lie detector. To use it on someone, you must touch the person, speak to them, and look them in the eyes. Test PERSUASION with a +1 (not an opposed roll). If you pass, you can tell if the person is lying or not.
Cost: 4,000 birr.

name: Morph
effect:
Your body is sculpted so that your entire physiognomy is changed – you could have anything from wings to extra limbs. This gives you obvious benefits, but could trigger fear and disgust among common people, or even hate among fanatics.
EXTRA PAIR OF ARMS: You can perform an extra fast action per turn, as long as you can use the extra arms for that action.
EXTRA FINGERS: You can use tools, make repairs, operate computers or do other tasks that require fine motor skills with extraordinary ease. You get a +1 in situations where fine motor skills are paramount, such as advanced MEDICAL AID, repairing precision engineering with TECHNOLOGY, or reprogramming a computer using DATA DJINN. Unfortunately, your brittle and sensitive fingers give you a -2 to FORCE.
WINGS: You can glide up to Long Range if you leap from at least 20 meters up. Test MOBILITY to land without taking damage (failure means D6 points of damage). When on the ground, you suffer a -1 to MOBILITY, due to the size of the wings.
PREHENSILE TAIL: You get a +2 to MOBILITY when climbing or moving around in low or zero-G. The tail is easily hidden under a coat or a caftan.
Cost: between 30,000 and 60,000 birr.

name: Nimble
effect:
Your bionically enhanced nerves give you amazing agility. You get a +1 to MOBILITY for acrobatic feats and gymnastic maneuvers. The modifier also applies to dance and other physical activities.
Cost: 15,000 birr.

name: Passive Sensor
effect:
Passive sensors are implanted in your body. You can use them like the passive mode on a personal sensor whenever you wish. Details for sensors are found in Equipment.
Cost: 2,000 birr

name: Quick Reflexes
effect:
Your muscles are bionically altered for incredibly explosive speed, making you a fast runner. Your Movement Rate is increased by 1 hex for a fast action per round (can be combined with Sprinter but not with Cybernetic Muscles). You can jump 5 meters horizontally from standing still, 15 meters with a running start (slow action), and 2 meters vertically.
Cost: 10,000 birr.

name: Regenerate
effect:
You heal fast, and recover remarkably quickly even from grave injuries. The time to heal a critical injury (page 94) is halved. You also get 1 extra Hit Capacity.
Cost: 15,000 birr.

name: Servo Locks
effect:
The joints in your arms and shoulders have been replaced with lockable servo units, enabling you to carry extremely heavy objects for short distances, and grapple people in combat very effectively. You get a +1 to MELEE COMBAT when your opponent tries to break free from your grappling hold, and a +1 to FORCE for heavy lifting.
Cost: 4,000 birr.

name: Skin Electrodes
effect:
Your palms are fitted with conductive surfaces capable of transmitting powerful electrical shocks. After a successful unarmed attack, you can choose to inflict shock damage instead of physical damage. Each additional six rolled inflicts 1 extra point of damage as normal.
Cost: 6,000 birr.

name: Targeting Scope
effect:
One of your eyes has been enhanced with a targeting scope. Makes it easier to hit with firearms (+1 to RANGED COMBAT) at Short range and above. Does not work for quick shots.
Cost: 20,000 birr.

name: Voice Amplifier
effect:
A resonance chamber with built-in loudspeakers in your throat can amplify your voice. You get a +1 to COMMAND or PERSUASION in situations where a loud voice is a benefit, for example when intimidating someone.
Cost: 2,000 birr.

name: Water Breathing
effect:
Artificial gills allow you to extract oxygen from water. You can remain under water for as long as you like but are affected by other factors like cold.
Cost: 5,000 birr.

name: Weatherproof
effect:
You are heavily modified to withstand all climates, recycle body fluids and conserve energy. The effect of this is that the time between each point of damage you suffer from thirst or hunger (page 98) is doubled – to 24 hours and 4 days, respectively.
Cost: 2,000 birr.

name: Artificer
effect: You can enter a trance to understand an artifact close to you, and to determine its origin and use.

name: Clairvoyant
effect: You get visions of where an object or a person can be found. The GM decides what form the visions take, but as a rule of thumb, an object you once owned is easier to locate than an object only described to you.

name: Exorcist
effect: You can enter a trance and exorcise an intruding spirit from someone.

name: Intuition
effect: You get to ask the GM a simple yes/no question about anything in the game world. He must answer truthfully “yes”, “no” or “maybe”. The GM can answer “maybe” even if he knows the answer, if he thinks answering yes or no would upset the game too much. Please note that neither truths nor lies are universal – it depends on who is asking. Opinions, morals and worldviews can make something true to someone and false to someone else.

name: Materia Shield
effect: You can attract loose objects and fragile matter by force of will, turning the attracted matter into a shield around you (armor 1 against ranged attacks and fire). Each extra six on your mystic powers roll adds 1 to the armor rating of the shield or allows you to protect one extra person within Close Range. People may attempt to force their way through the shield by rolling an opposed FORCE vs your armor rating (need success equal or greater than armor rating). Creating the shield is a Slow action and maintaining it is a Fast action per turn. When taking damage, roll a CUF roll and on failure, you lose concentration, dropping the shield. If you fail to maintain the shield by using an action, the effect stops and must be done once again.

name: Mind Reader
effect: You can read someone else’s thoughts for a minute or so. You can only read surface thoughts; you can’t dig for any deeper memories. Your target must be within Close Range. Failure means the target is aware of a presence in their mind.

name: Mind Walker
effect: If you focus your thoughts on a person you have previously met, you can tap into that person’s sensory input. You experience what that person sees, hears and feels in that exact moment, regardless of where in the Horizon thy are. No thoughts or emotions are transmitted

name: Prediction
effect: If you conduct a séance, you can experience powerful visions of the future. You ask the GM questions about yourself or someone else taking part in the séance. The GM answers as best he can. The answers should be short, preferably mysterious and ambiguous. An answer could also take the form of an omen, a sign of fortune or tragedy waiting around the corner.

name: Premonition
effect: In some mysterious way, you can sense impending danger. The GM will have you test MYSTIC POWERS – if you pass, you get a feeling of a looming threat, but no details about what it might be.

name: Puppeteer
effect: Using a Slow action, you may assume control over a person you have known for some time or have shared a traumatic experience with. Your target may let you control her or try to resist. Resisting is an opposed EMPATHY or COMMAND vs your MYSTIC POWERS roll. You get a -1 if your target is out of sight but on the same planet as you, and a -3 if she is further away than that but still in the same system. Maintaining control is one Slow action per turn. If the person you are controlling suffers damage, you immediately suffer 1 point of stress. If your target becomes Broken, you suffer 2 points of stress and the connection is severed.

name: Stop
effect: You can stop an NPC from performing an action they otherwise would have. It must be something subtle, that can be attributed to simple forgetfulness. Typical examples would be that the NPC lets the PCs pass a roadblock without checking their papers, or forgets their keys somewhere. The power cannot be used to stop an incoming attack. The target will find the interaction odd and will remember they did this, but not understand why which may draw attention later.

name: Telekinesis
effect: You can lift, move, turn or bend an object using sheer force of will. The item must be tiny – larger objects are beyond your control. No dice roll is needed, unless you want to use the object for something demanding like moving a key to a lock and then turning it. Then test any appropriate skill. The power cannot be used to attack someone in combat.

name: Telekinetic Blast
effect: At the cost of 1 Stress, you can create a telekinetic blast that can knock over objects (weapon damage 2, CRIT 3, Short range only).

name: Telepathy
effect: You can also transmit short telepathic messages. When stressed, your thoughts sometimes spill over into the heads of those nearby, especially other mystics.

name: Thought Transference
effect: You can project your thoughts into the minds of other people in sight. The recipient automatically understands that the thoughts came from you. Extra sixes on your mystic powers roll allow you to communicate with your PC Buddy regardless of distance or project your thoughts onto one extra person per six. A critically successful roll allows you to communicate with a person you know somewhat well regardless of distance.
